validity.recommendation: Do NOT fill Operator with 'GSPL India Gasnet Limited (GIGL)' from the wiki. GIGL's authorisation for this exact 725 km corridor (granted to GSPL 07.07.2011, target completion 06.07.2014) was foreclosed by PNGRB north of Gurdaspur after GIGL/GSPL failed to complete the pipeline up to Srinagar; PNGRB disqualified GIGL and its lead partner GSPL from re-bidding, and GAIL (India) Ltd won the re-let Gurdaspur-Jammu piece in June 2023 (this brief's P5413). The other surviving piece of GIGL's original grant, Bhatinda-Gurdaspur, is tracked separately (P3913/P5533) and already has its own owner/operator question staged in the register-crosswalk leg. Filling Operator=GIGL on this 725 km row would restate a cancelled mandate as a current one. Whether P0908 itself should be retired/reclassified now that GEM carries the successor rows is a call for the redundancy-adjudication leg (already run, not re-litigated here) -- this finding is only that the wiki's Operator value is unsafe to apply as-is.
validity.researcher_notes: Searched for the PNGRB foreclosure history. psuwatch.com (22 Jun 2023, PTI-sourced) states plainly: 'Originally, the Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar natural gas pipeline was awarded to Gujarat State Petronet Ltd (GSPL)-led consortium, which later on registered as a company named GSPL India Gasnet Ltd (GIGL). However, GIGL failed to lay the pipeline within the stipulated time, following which PNGRB cancelled the authorisation and suo-motu invited bids for the Gurdaspur-Jammu line... PNGRB disqualified GIGL and its lead partner GSPL from submitting a bid for the proposed pipeline.' The identical text is carried by Business Standard (archived, business-standard.com live-403s but the Wayback snapshot confirms the same PTI wire text) -- same origin as psuwatch, so NOT counted as a second independent source; tier medium. Earlier reporting (greaterkashmir.com, 2018, 'Bhatinda-Srinagar gas pipeline project mired in 7-year old bottleneck') shows GIGL still describing the project as ongoing-in-stages at that date -- i.e. GEM's 'proposed' framing on P0908 matches the PRE-foreclosure narrative, consistent with the brief's note that this row 'still carries the foreclosed framing.'

validity.recommendation: Leave StartYear1 blank. The wiki's 'Unknown' is not a usable value, and independent sources confirm the pipeline was never commissioned under this 725 km authorisation: the original 6 July 2014 completion target was missed, the project was still 'ongoing in stages' with no fixed new timeline as of 2018 (greaterkashmir.com), and PNGRB ultimately foreclosed the corridor north of Gurdaspur rather than the line ever being commissioned end-to-end. Status='proposed' with StartYear1 blank is the correct pairing.
validity.researcher_notes: greaterkashmir.com (2018) quotes a GIGL official: the project 'which was kick-started in 2011' had not been abandoned but was stalled pending a J&K Gas Pipeline Act amendment, with the 2016 GSPL-state MoU itself delayed. psuwatch.com (2023) confirms the eventual outcome was foreclosure/cancellation, not commissioning. No source anywhere reports a commissioning date for the full Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar line -- because it never happened.

validity.recommendation: Do NOT change LengthKnownKm to match the drawn route. Independent press corroborates 725 km for the original Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar authorisation (route through Kathua, Samba, Jammu, Udhampur, Ramban, Anantnag and Srinagar districts) -- the sheet's value is well supported. The drawn geometry (464 km, RouteAccuracy=medium) undershoots the true corridor, most likely because it draws only part of the route (plausibly stopping short of Srinagar, or capturing only the section GIGL actually progressed before foreclosure) rather than the full 725 km grant. Flag for route review/redraw, not a length correction.
validity.researcher_notes: greaterkashmir.com: 'The original completion date for laying the 725 km long pipeline project was July 6, 2014,' with the route running 'from Bhatinda in Punjab to Srinagar via Jammu' through the seven named districts. A second greaterkashmir.com piece ('Government to fix timeline for project completion') repeats the 725 km figure but is the same publisher, so treated as one strong source (tier medium), not two independent ones, per the corroboration rule.
